fixtures: No files and no network: web tools are disabled in eval runs, so each case asks for the fetch plan (which sources, in what order, and why) rather than the fetched content.

evals.name: cursor-docs-rate-limited
evals.prompt: I'm doing the vendor sync and cursor.com/docs keeps returning 429 to the fetcher. Where do I get current Cursor plugin format info instead? I can't fetch anything from this session, so just tell me the sources in order and what to do if they fail too.
evals.expected_output: Cursor's docs rate-limit programmatic access, so use the fallback order: 1) https://github.com/cursor/plugin-template (README and example files), 2) https://github.com/cursor/plugins (official plugin examples), 3) the forum thread https://forum.cursor.com/t/support-for-agent-folder-compatibility/154167 on agents/ folder support. Prefer GitHub raw content. If all three fail or are incomplete, flag the gap explicitly in the sync report; do not silently leave Cursor out.
assertions: Gives github.com/cursor/plugin-template as the first source
Gives github.com/cursor/plugins as the second source
Gives the forum thread forum.cursor.com/t/support-for-agent-folder-compatibility/154167 as the third source
Says that if all of them fail, the gap is flagged explicitly in the report rather than Cursor being silently skipped
Does not recommend third-party blogs, tutorials or community mirrors as a source

evals.name: marketplace-source-recheck
evals.prompt: Vendor sync time. Before I fetch anything: which doc pages and trackers should I pull to see whether Claude Code and Copilot CLI still disagree on marketplace source types? Give me the URLs in order; I'll fetch them myself.
evals.expected_output: The marketplace source-type tables in both Claude Code's plugin-marketplaces doc (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces) and Copilot's CLI plugin reference (https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference). The /reference/ pages beat the /how-tos/ pages when they disagree. Plus the upstream trackers: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/issues/1205 and https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues. Explains why: the divergence is fatal, because one unsupported source entry breaks a whole index.
assertions: Names Copilot's cli-plugin-reference page under docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/
Names Claude Code's plugin-marketplaces doc on code.claude.com
Names the github/copilot-cli repository (its issues) as a tracker to check
Says to prefer Copilot's /reference/ pages over its /how-tos/ pages when they disagree
Explains that one unsupported source entry breaks the whole marketplace index

evals.name: codex-hooks-redirect
evals.prompt: Fetching developers.openai.com/codex/hooks bounced me to learn.chatgpt.com. Is that legit, and which sources should the Codex part of the sync use? No network here, just the plan.
evals.expected_output: The redirect is expected: developers.openai.com/codex/* now redirects to learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*. The Codex sources are https://developers.openai.com/codex/plugins, https://developers.openai.com/codex/plugins/build, https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks and the https://github.com/openai/codex README, preferring GitHub raw content where it exists. Report any fetch failure clearly instead of skipping Codex, and structure the output vendor, then artifact type, then current content.
assertions: Says the developers.openai.com/codex to learn.chatgpt.com redirect is expected
Lists the Codex plugins, plugins/build and hooks pages on developers.openai.com
Says to prefer GitHub raw content where available
Says fetch failures are reported, not silently skipped
Structures the output by vendor, then artifact type, then content
